literature_notes: FAP (Prolyl endopeptidase FAP, UniProt P97321/Q12884) is a Type II single-pass transmembrane protein. Its topology places residues 1–6 intracellularly, residues 7–26 in the TM helix, and residues 27–760 in the large extracellular ectodomain. The sole ledger line, L1, describes a 'FAP-targeted CAR construct' bearing an N-terminal Myc tag for flow-cytometry surface detection. This fails on two independent grounds. First, the tagged entity is the CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) construct itself — a synthetic receptor designed to recognise FAP as its antigen — not full-length membrane-anchored FAP. The Myc tag confirms surface display of the CAR, not of FAP. Second, even if the clip were re-read as tagging FAP directly, the N-terminus of FAP (residues 1–6) is intracellular; an N-terminal tag on FAP would face the cytoplasm and is not an extracellular surface tag. No snorkel validation is mentioned. Neither reading yields a qualifying extracellular insertion site on FAP. No other ledger lines are provided. The result is zero sites, which is the correct answer given the evidence.
